mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced consumer and business spending, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2 percentage points in the past month indicates a weakening labor market, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE rises by >0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the past month signals strong demand in the housing market, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when HOUST increases by >5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past two months indicates increased supply and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 0.5% but is accompanied by a larger increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL), it indicates inflationary pressures that could negatively impact S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 growth < CPIAUCSL growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases but the unemployment rate (UNRATE) does not decrease, it indicates labor market inefficiency, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE does not decrease
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE does not decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real federal surplus (RSAFS) by more than $10 billion in the past month indicates reduced government demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when RSAFS decreases by >$10bn, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) improve (PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases), it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.
